questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling under 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Use hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes based on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that gives you the most visibility and space around you. Move to a different position as traffic changes.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center portion of the lane:

options.text: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
Usually makes it difficult for the driver to see you.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of the lane places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because it places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if needed.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank to help your balance.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never try to go around a train.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation for keeping riders together while maintaining safe distance is generally:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group of motorcyclists stay close together while giving each rider enough space for safety.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: So the driver can see you in their side mirror.
So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
So the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the vehicle. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how quickly it was consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after consuming any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to make sure others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight and running lights on. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good road surface, you should:

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire locks on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to protect against engine and wind noise damage.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to protect against engine and wind noise damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to watch for changes in the road.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider always do to turn safely?

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: What about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Use it only when sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It usually provides good traction, unless it is raining.
Avoid it at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually provides good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, unless it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide. Riders can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.
